```
    35→ *   run_type?: 'gpu' | 'api',  // Optional service-role filter by execution environment
    36→ *   debug?: boolean            // Optional: enable verbose logging and extra queries
    37→ * }
    38→ *
    39→ * Returns:
    40→ * {
    41→ *   mode: 'count',
    42→ *   timestamp: string,
    43→ *   run_type_filter_requested?: 'gpu' | 'api' | null,
    44→ *   run_type_filter?: 'gpu' | 'api' | null,
    45→ *   // For PAT requests, run_type_filter is always null (filter not applied)
    46→ *
    47→ *   // Quick counts for scaling math (service role only)
    48→ *   totals: {
    49→ *     // Core counts (capacity-limited)
    50→ *     queued_only: number,             // Immediately claimable tasks (capacity-limited)
    51→ *     active_only: number,             // Tasks being processed
    52→ *     queued_plus_active: number,      // Total workload
    53→ *
    54→ *     // Breakdown for smarter scaling decisions (service role only)
    55→ *     blocked_by_capacity: number,     // Blocked by user's 5-task limit (will free up)
    56→ *     blocked_by_deps: number,         // Blocked by incomplete dependencies
    57→ *     blocked_by_settings: number,     // Blocked because user has cloud disabled
    58→ *     potentially_claimable: number,   // queued_only + blocked_by_capacity (for scaling)
    59→ *   },
    60→ *
    61→ *   // Detailed task arrays (limited to 100 for service role, 50 for user)
    62→ *   // Note: queued_tasks only includes immediately claimable tasks (matches queued_only criteria)
    63→ *   queued_tasks: [{...}],
    64→ *   active_tasks: [{...}],
    65→ *
    66→ *   // User stats (service role only)
    67→ *   users?: [...],
    68→ *
    69→ *   // User-specific info (user token only)
    70→ *   user_id?: string,
    71→ *   user_info?: {...}
    72→ * }
    73→ *
    74→ * - 200 OK with task count data
    75→ * - 401 Unauthorized if no valid token
    76→ * - 403 Forbidden if token invalid
    77→ * - 500 Internal Server Error
    78→ */
    79→serve(async (req) => {
    80→  const bootstrap = await bootstrapEdgeHandler(req, {
    81→    functionName: "task-counts",
    82→    logPrefix: "[TASK-COUNTS]",
    83→    parseBody: "loose",
    84→    auth: {
    85→      required: true,
    86→    },
    87→    ...NO_SESSION_RUNTIME_OPTIONS,
    88→  });
    89→  if (!bootstrap.ok) {
    90→    return bootstrap.response;
    91→  }
    92→
    93→  const { supabaseAdmin, logger, auth, body: requestBody } = bootstrap.value;
    94→  const requestedRunType = parseRunType(requestBody); // 'gpu', 'api', or null (no filtering)
    95→  const debug = parseDebug(requestBody); // Enable verbose logging
    96→
    97→  const startTime = Date.now();
    98→
    99→  const isServiceRole = auth?.isServiceRole === true;
   100→  const callerId = auth?.userId;
   101→  const appliedRunType = isServiceRole ? requestedRunType : null;
   102→
   103→  if (debug) {
   104→    if (isServiceRole) {
   105→      logger.debug("Authenticated via service-role key");
   106→    } else {
   107→      logger.debug("Authenticated via PAT", { user_id: callerId });
   108→      if (requestedRunType) {
   109→        logger.debug("Ignoring run_type filter for PAT request", { requested_run_type: requestedRunType });
   110→      }
   111→    }
   112→  }
   113→
   114→  try {
   115→    if (isServiceRole) {
   116→      // ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
   117→      // SERVICE ROLE PATH: Global task statistics across all users
   118→      // ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
   119→
   120→      // ESSENTIAL: Get counts from RPC functions (4 parallel calls)
   121→      const [countQueuedOnly, countQueuedPlusActive, breakdownResult, userStatsResult] = await Promise.all([
   122→        supabaseAdmin.rpc('count_eligible_tasks_service_role', { p_include_active: false, p_run_type: appliedRunType }),
   123→        supabaseAdmin.rpc('count_eligible_tasks_service_role', { p_include_active: true, p_run_type: appliedRunType }),
   124→        supabaseAdmin.rpc('count_queued_tasks_breakdown_service_role', { p_run_type: appliedRunType }),
   125→        supabaseAdmin.rpc('per_user_capacity_stats_service_role')
   126→      ]);
   127→
   128→      if (countQueuedOnly.error) {
   129→        logger.error("Service role count (queued only) error", { error: countQueuedOnly.error.message });
   130→        throw countQueuedOnly.error;
   131→      }
   132→      if (countQueuedPlusActive.error) {
   133→        logger.error("Service role count (queued+active) error", { error: countQueuedPlusActive.error.message });
   134→        throw countQueuedPlusActive.error;
   135→      }
   136→      if (breakdownResult.error) {
   137→        logger.error("Service role breakdown error", { error: breakdownResult.error.message });
   138→        throw breakdownResult.error;
   139→      }
   140→
   141→      // Legacy capacity-limited counts (for backward compatibility and claim logic)
   142→      const queued_only = countQueuedOnly.data ?? 0;
   143→      const queued_plus_active = countQueuedPlusActive.data ?? 0;
   144→      const active_only = Math.max(0, queued_plus_active - queued_only);
   145→
   146→      // Extract breakdown for scaling decisions (RPC returns a single row)
   147→      // Note: breakdown counts are per-task eligibility, not capacity-limited
   148→      const breakdown = breakdownResult.data?.[0] ?? {
   149→        claimable_now: 0,
   150→        blocked_by_capacity: 0,
   151→        blocked_by_deps: 0,
   152→        blocked_by_settings: 0,
   153→        total_queued: 0
   154→      };
   155→
   156→      const blocked_by_capacity = breakdown.blocked_by_capacity ?? 0;
   157→      const blocked_by_deps = breakdown.blocked_by_deps ?? 0;
   158→      const blocked_by_settings = breakdown.blocked_by_settings ?? 0;
   159→      // For scaling: tasks that will become claimable as capacity frees up
   160→      // Use queued_only (capacity-limited) + tasks explicitly blocked by capacity
   161→      const potentially_claimable = queued_only + blocked_by_capacity;
   162→
   163→      // Format user stats
   164→      const user_stats = Array.isArray(userStatsResult.data)
   165→        ? userStatsResult.data.map((u: unknown) => ({
   166→            user_id: u.user_id,
   167→            credits: u.credits,
   168→            queued_tasks: u.queued_tasks,
   169→            in_progress_tasks: u.in_progress_tasks,
   170→            allows_cloud: u.allows_cloud,
   171→            at_limit: u.at_limit
   172→          }))
   173→        : [];
   174→
   175→      // Fetch task_types lookup if run_type filtering is needed
   176→      let taskTypeRunTypeMap: Map<string, string> | null = null;
   177→      if (appliedRunType) {
   178→        const { data: taskTypes } = await supabaseAdmin
   179→          .from('task_types')
   180→          .select('name, run_type')
   181→          .eq('is_active', true);
   182→
   183→        if (taskTypes) {
   184→          taskTypeRunTypeMap = new Map(taskTypes.map(tt => [tt.name, tt.run_type]));
   185→        }
   186→      }
   187→
   188→      // Build map of user in-progress counts for capacity filtering
   189→      const userInProgressMap = new Map<string, number>();
   190→      if (Array.isArray(userStatsResult.data)) {
   191→        for (const u of userStatsResult.data) {
   192→          userInProgressMap.set(u.user_id, u.in_progress_tasks ?? 0);
   193→        }
   194→      }
   195→
   196→      // Fetch detailed task lists (parallel, with limits for performance)
   197→      const [queuedResult, activeResult] = await Promise.all([
   198→        supabaseAdmin
   199→          .from('tasks')
   200→          .select(`
   201→            id,
   202→            task_type,
   203→            created_at,
   204→            dependant_on,
   205→            projects!inner(user_id, users!inner(credits, settings))
   206→          `)
   207→          .eq('status', 'Queued')
   208→          .order('created_at', { ascending: true })
   209→          .limit(100),
   210→        supabaseAdmin
   211→          .from('tasks')
   212→          .select(`
   213→            id,
   214→            task_type,
   215→            worker_id,
   216→            updated_at,
   217→            projects!inner(user_id, users!inner(credits, settings))
   218→          `)
   219→          .eq('status', 'In Progress')
   220→          .not('worker_id', 'is', null)
   221→          .order('updated_at', { ascending: true })
   222→          .limit(100)
   223→      ]);
   224→
   225→      // Collect all dependency task IDs to check their completion status
   226→      const allDepIds = new Set<string>();
   227→      for (const task of queuedResult.data || []) {
   228→        if (Array.isArray(task.dependant_on)) {
   229→          for (const depId of task.dependant_on) {
   230→            allDepIds.add(depId);
   231→          }
   232→        }
   233→      }
   234→
   235→      // Fetch dependency task statuses if any
   236→      const completedDepIds = new Set<string>();
   237→      if (allDepIds.size > 0) {
   238→        const { data: depTasks } = await supabaseAdmin
   239→          .from('tasks')
   240→          .select('id, status')
   241→          .in('id', Array.from(allDepIds));
   242→
   243→        if (depTasks) {
   244→          for (const dep of depTasks) {
   245→            if (dep.status === 'Complete') {
   246→              completedDepIds.add(dep.id);
   247→            }
   248→          }
   249→        }
   250→      }
   251→
   252→      // Helper to check if all dependencies are complete
   253→      const allDepsComplete = (dependant_on: string[] | null): boolean => {
   254→        if (!dependant_on || dependant_on.length === 0) return true;
   255→        return dependant_on.every(depId => completedDepIds.has(depId));
   256→      };
   257→
   258→      // Filter queued tasks to match RPC criteria (only claimable tasks)
   259→      // Criteria: not orchestrator, credits > 0, allows_cloud, deps complete, user not at capacity
   260→      const queued_tasks = (queuedResult.data || [])
   261→        .filter(task => {
   262→          // Exclude orchestrator tasks
   263→          if (task.task_type?.toLowerCase().includes('orchestrator')) return false;
   264→          // Exclude no-credits users
   265→          if (task.projects.users.credits <= 0) return false;
   266→          // Exclude users with cloud disabled
   267→          const allowsCloud = task.projects.users.settings?.ui?.generationMethods?.inCloud ?? true;
   268→          if (!allowsCloud) return false;
   269→          // Exclude tasks with incomplete dependencies
   270→          if (!allDepsComplete(task.dependant_on)) return false;

   272→          const userInProgress = userInProgressMap.get(task.projects.user_id) ?? 0;
   273→          if (userInProgress >= 5) return false;

   277→            if (!taskRunType || taskRunType !== appliedRunType) return false;
   278→          }
   279→          return true;
   280→        })
   281→        .map(task => ({
   282→          task_id: task.id,
   283→          task_type: task.task_type,
   284→          user_id: task.projects.user_id,
   285→          created_at: task.created_at
   286→        }));
   287→
   288→      // Filter active tasks (orchestrator, credits, run_type, api-worker exclusion)
   289→      const active_tasks = (activeResult.data || [])
   290→        .filter(task => {
   291→          if (task.task_type?.toLowerCase().includes('orchestrator')) return false;
   292→          if (task.projects.users.credits <= 0) return false;
   293→          if (appliedRunType === 'gpu' && task.worker_id === 'api-worker-main') return false;
   294→          if (appliedRunType && taskTypeRunTypeMap) {

   299→        })
   300→        .map(task => ({

   313→          potentially_claimable, active_only,

   319→        // Validation warnings (array may differ due to 100-task limit or race conditions)

   323→      }

   325→      const elapsed = Date.now() - startTime;

   328→      }
   329→
   330→      return new Response(JSON.stringify({
   331→        mode: 'count',
   332→        timestamp: new Date().toISOString(),
   333→        run_type_filter_requested: requestedRunType,

   335→        totals: {

   354→    } else {
   355→      // ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
   356→      // USER TOKEN PATH: Task statistics for specific user

   358→
   359→      // ESSENTIAL: Get counts, user info, and project IDs (4 parallel calls)
   360→      const [countQueuedOnly, countQueuedPlusActive, analysisResult, projectsResult] = await Promise.all([
   361→        supabaseAdmin.rpc('count_eligible_tasks_user_pat', { p_user_id: callerId, p_include_active: false }),
   362→        supabaseAdmin.rpc('count_eligible_tasks_user_pat', { p_user_id: callerId, p_include_active: true }),
   363→        supabaseAdmin.rpc('analyze_task_availability_user_pat', { p_user_id: callerId, p_include_active: true }),
   364→        supabaseAdmin.from('projects').select('id').eq('user_id', callerId)
   365→      ]);
   366→
   367→      if (countQueuedOnly.error) {

   370→      }
   371→      if (countQueuedPlusActive.error) {
   372→        logger.error("User count (queued+active) error", { error: countQueuedPlusActive.error.message, user_id: callerId });
   373→        throw countQueuedPlusActive.error;
   374→      }
   375→
   376→      const queued_only = countQueuedOnly.data ?? 0;
   377→      const queued_plus_active = countQueuedPlusActive.data ?? 0;
   378→      const active_only = Math.max(0, queued_plus_active - queued_only);
   379→
   380→      const analysis = analysisResult.data || {};
   381→      const eligible_queued = analysis.eligible_count ?? 0;
   382→      const user_info = analysis.user_info ?? {};
   383→
   384→      const projectIds = projectsResult.data?.map(p => p.id) || [];
   385→
   386→      let queued_tasks: unknown[] = [];
   387→      let active_tasks: unknown[] = [];
   388→
   389→      if (projectIds.length > 0) {
   390→        // Fetch task details (parallel)
   391→        const [queuedResult, activeResult] = await Promise.all([
   392→          supabaseAdmin
   393→            .from('tasks')
   394→            .select('id, task_type, created_at, project_id')
   395→            .eq('status', 'Queued')
   396→            .in('project_id', projectIds)
   397→            .order('created_at', { ascending: true })
   398→            .limit(50),
   399→          supabaseAdmin
   400→            .from('tasks')
   401→            .select('id, task_type, worker_id, updated_at, project_id')
   402→            .eq('status', 'In Progress')
   403→            .in('project_id', projectIds)
   404→            .not('worker_id', 'is', null)
   405→            .order('updated_at', { ascending: true })
   406→            .limit(50)
   407→        ]);

   409→        // Filter and format queued tasks
   410→        queued_tasks = (queuedResult.data || [])
   411→          .filter(task => !task.task_type?.toLowerCase().includes('orchestrator'))
   412→          .map(task => ({
   413→            task_id: task.id,
   414→            task_type: task.task_type,
   415→            user_id: callerId,
   416→            created_at: task.created_at
   417→          }));
   418→
   419→        // Filter and format active tasks
   420→        active_tasks = (activeResult.data || [])
   421→          .filter(task => !task.task_type?.toLowerCase().includes('orchestrator'))
   422→          .map(task => ({
   423→            task_id: task.id,
   424→            task_type: task.task_type,
   425→            worker_id: task.worker_id,
   426→            user_id: callerId,
   427→            started_at: task.updated_at
   428→          }));
   429→      }
   430→
   431→      if (debug) {
   432→        logger.debug('User counts', { user_id: callerId, queued_only, active_only, eligible_queued });
   433→      }
   434→
   435→      const elapsed = Date.now() - startTime;
   436→
   437→      return new Response(JSON.stringify({
   438→        mode: 'count',

   440→        user_id: callerId,
   441→        run_type_filter_requested: requestedRunType,
   442→        run_type_filter: appliedRunType,
   443→        totals: {

   456→        },
   457→        elapsed_ms: debug ? elapsed : undefined
   458→      }), {
   459→        status: 200,
   460→        headers: { "Content-Type": "application/json" }
   461→      });
   462→    }
   463→  } catch (error: unknown) {
   464→    const message = toErrorMessage(error);
   465→    logger.error("Unexpected error", { error: message });
   466→    await logger.flush();
   467→    return new Response(`Internal server error: ${message}`, { status: 500 });
   468→  }
   469→});
   470→
```

```
1→/**
     2→ * useReplaceInShot Hook
     3→ *
     4→ * Handles swapping timeline position from a parent generation to the current image.
     5→ * Used when user wants to replace a parent image in the timeline with a derived image.
     6→ */
     7→
     8→import { useCallback } from 'react';
     9→import { normalizeAndPresentError } from '@/shared/lib/errorHandling/runtimeError';
    10→import { getSupabaseClient as supabase } from '@/integrations/supabase/client';
    11→
    12→interface UseReplaceInShotProps {
    13→  /** Callback to close the lightbox after successful replacement */
    14→  onClose: () => void;
    15→}
    16→
    17→interface UseReplaceInShotReturn {
    18→  /**
    19→   * Replace parent's timeline position with current image
    20→   * @param parentGenerationId - ID of the parent generation to remove from timeline
    21→   * @param currentMediaId - ID of the current media to place in timeline
    22→   * @param parentTimelineFrame - Timeline frame position to use
    23→   * @param shotId - Shot ID for the replacement
    24→   */
    25→  handleReplaceInShot: (
    26→    parentGenerationId: string,
    27→    currentMediaId: string,
    28→    parentTimelineFrame: number,
    29→    shotId: string
    30→  ) => Promise<void>;
    31→}
    32→
    33→export function useReplaceInShot({
    34→  onClose,
    35→}: UseReplaceInShotProps): UseReplaceInShotReturn {
    36→  const handleReplaceInShot = useCallback(async (
    37→    parentGenerationId: string,
    38→    currentMediaId: string,
    39→    parentTimelineFrame: number,
    40→    shotIdParam: string
    41→  ) => {
    42→
    43→    try {
    44→      // 1. Remove timeline_frame from parent's shot_generation record
    45→      const { error: removeError } = await supabase().from('shot_generations')
    46→        .update({ timeline_frame: null })
    47→        .eq('generation_id', parentGenerationId)
    48→        .eq('shot_id', shotIdParam);
    49→
    50→      if (removeError) throw removeError;
    51→
    52→      // 2. Update or create shot_generation for current image with the timeline_frame
    53→      // First check if current image already has a shot_generation for this shot
    54→      const { data: existingAssoc } = await supabase().from('shot_generations')
    55→        .select('id')
    56→        .eq('generation_id', currentMediaId)
    57→        .eq('shot_id', shotIdParam)
    58→        .single();
    59→
    60→      if (existingAssoc) {
    61→        // Update existing
    62→        const { error: updateError } = await supabase().from('shot_generations')
    63→          .update({
    64→            timeline_frame: parentTimelineFrame,
    65→            metadata: { user_positioned: true, drag_source: 'replace_parent' }
    66→          })
    67→          .eq('id', existingAssoc.id);
    68→
    69→        if (updateError) throw updateError;
    70→      } else {
    71→        // Create new
    72→        const { error: createError } = await supabase().from('shot_generations')
    73→          .insert({
    74→            shot_id: shotIdParam,
    75→            generation_id: currentMediaId,
    76→            timeline_frame: parentTimelineFrame,
    77→            metadata: { user_positioned: true, drag_source: 'replace_parent' }
    78→          });
    79→
    80→        if (createError) throw createError;
    81→      }
    82→
    83→      // Close lightbox to force refresh when reopened
    84→      onClose();
    85→    } catch (error) {
    86→      normalizeAndPresentError(error, { context: 'useReplaceInShot', showToast: false });
    87→      return;
    88→    }
    89→  }, [onClose]);
    90→
    91→  return { handleReplaceInShot };
    92→}
    93→
```

```
    68→
    69→  return signatures.some(sig => sig.split('=')[1] === signature_hex);
```

**Summary of findings (14 defects identified):**

The codebase has solid fundamentals -- clear naming, consistent error handling patterns, good use of TypeScript, and well-structured utility functions (e.g., `timelineFrameCalculators.ts`, `DataFreshnessManager.ts`, `costHelpers.ts`). Edge function code (`generation.ts`, `orchestratorCore.ts`) is particularly well-structured with clean routing and error handling.

However, there are recurring patterns that drag down low-level elegance:

1. **Reshape layers without value** (3 findings): Multiple files exist solely to copy fields between isomorphic object shapes -- `useShotEditorLayoutPayloadModel` (340 lines of pure reshaping), `buildInlineEditCanvasModel`/`buildInlineEditSidebarModel`, and similar patterns. These add indirection without logic.

2. **Monolithic orchestrator hooks** (3 findings): `useInlineEditState` (367 lines wiring 10+ hooks), `MediaGallery` (290 lines of hook calls before JSX), and `ImageLightbox`'s render model all suffer from being single functions that manually thread state between many sub-hooks.

3. **Repetitive boilerplate** (2 findings): `useGenerationMutations` repeats the same 5-step scope-verify-execute-check pattern 4 times, and `useEditSettingsPersistence` has 10 nearly identical dual-write useCallback wrappers.

4. **Control flow opacity** (3 findings): Nested ternaries for segment slot resolution, 15+ conditional spread expressions in payload builders, and a long if/else-if chain in ProductTour.

5. **Convention violations** (1 finding): Hardcoded color classes in LightboxLayout violate the project's own CLAUDE.md rule.

```
   343→  if (typeof firstArg === 'string') {
   344→    const tagMatch = firstArg.match(/^\[([^\]]+)\]$/);
   345→    if (tagMatch) {
   346→      tag = tagMatch[1];
   347→      messageArgs = args.slice(1);
   348→    } else if (firstArg.startsWith('[') && firstArg.includes(']')) {
   349→      // Handle "[Tag] message" format
   350→      const fullMatch = firstArg.match(/^\[([^\]]+)\]\s*(.*)/);
   351→      if (fullMatch) {
   352→        tag = fullMatch[1];
   353→        messageArgs = fullMatch[2] ? [fullMatch[2], ...args.slice(1)] : args.slice(1);
   354→      }
   355→    }
   356→  }
   357→  
   358→  // Serialize args safely
   359→  const message = `[${tag}] ${messageArgs.map(arg => {
   360→    try {
   361→      if (typeof arg === 'string') return arg;
   362→      if (arg instanceof Error) return `${arg.name}: ${arg.message}`;
   363→      return JSON.stringify(arg);
   364→    } catch {
   365→      return String(arg);
   366→    }
   367→  }).join(' ')}`;
   368→  
   369→  logBuffer.push({
   370→    timestamp: new Date().toISOString(),
   371→    source_type: 'browser',
   372→    source_id: SESSION_ID,
   373→    log_level: level,
   374→    message: message.slice(0, 2000), // Truncate very long messages
   375→    task_id: null,
   376→    metadata: {
   377→      user_id: getUserId(),
   378→      url: typeof window !== 'undefined' ? window.location.pathname : null,
   379→    }
   380→  });
   381→  
   382→  // Flush if buffer is full
   383→  if (logBuffer.length >= FLUSH_BUFFER_SIZE) {
   384→    flushLogs();
   385→  } else if (!isFlushScheduled) {
   386→    scheduleFlush();
```

Now let me look at a few more areas for contract issues. Let me check the `createGenerationFromTask` function signature vs its declared `authContext` parameter:

In `generation.ts`, `createGenerationFromTask` has `authContext: CompletionAuthContext` as the 7th positional parameter (line 207). But looking at the signature:
```ts
export async function createGenerationFromTask(
  supabase: SupabaseClient,
  taskId: string,
  taskData: unknown,
  publicUrl: string,
  thumbnailUrl: string | null | undefined,
  logger?: CompletionLogger,
  authContext: CompletionAuthContext,
): Promise<GenerationCreationOutcome>
```

The `logger` parameter is optional (`logger?`), followed by a required `authContext`. This means if a caller passes 6 args (omitting logger), `authContext` would be the 7th positional arg and would be `undefined`. This is a problematic positional signature: an optional parameter before a required one. TypeScript should catch this at call sites, but the pattern is a contract smell.

5. **Edit settings dual-persistence forwarding** (high) - 12 `useCallback` wrappers in `useEditSettingsPersistence` that each forward to one setter plus optionally call `updateLastUsed`, with several being pure passthroughs.

6. **Task payload contract layering** (medium) - 4 layers of task contract composition where some modules (like `taskFieldPolicy.ts` at 24 lines) are almost pure re-exports.

7. **composeOptionalFields ceremony** (medium) - Abstraction used for optional field assignment that's more verbose than the inline conditional spread it replaces.

8. **Singleton class pattern** (low) - `PreloadingService` uses Java-style `private constructor + static getInstance()` where a simple `new` export works (as seen in `DataFreshnessManager`).

9. **Parallel payload builders** (medium) - `segmentTaskPayload.ts` builds overlapping payloads with duplicated field assignments across `buildOrchestratorDetails` and `buildTaskParamsPayload`.

The codebase has solid fundamentals -- clear naming, consistent error handling patterns, good use of TypeScript, and well-structured utility functions (e.g., `timelineFrameCalculators.ts`, `DataFreshnessManager.ts`, `costHelpers.ts`). Edge function code (`generation.ts`, `orchestratorCore.ts`) is particularly well-structured with clean routing and error handling.

These add indirection without logic.

2. **Monolithic orchestrator hooks** (3 findings): `useInlineEditState` (367 lines wiring 10+ hooks), `MediaGallery` (290 lines of hook calls before JSX), and `ImageLightbox`'s render model all suffer from being single functions that manually thread state between many sub-hooks.

3. **Repetitive boilerplate** (2 findings): `useGenerationMutations` repeats the same 5-step scope-verify-execute-check pattern 4 times, and `useEditSettingsPersistence` has 10 nearly identical dual-write useCallback wrappers.

4. **Control flow opacity** (3 findings): Nested ternaries for segment slot resolution, 15+ conditional spread expressions in payload builders, and a long if/else-if chain in ProductTour.

5. **Convention violations** (1 finding): Hardcoded color classes in LightboxLayout violate the project's own CLAUDE.md rule.</result>

```
1→# Frontend Architecture Patterns
     2→
     3→---
     4→
     5→## State Management
     6→
     7→No Redux/Zustand. State flows through specific layers:
     8→
     9→| Layer | Tool | Purpose |
    10→|-------|------|---------|
    11→| **Server state** | React Query | Remote data (shots, generations, settings) |
    12→| **Query keys** | `queryKeys` registry (`shared/lib/queryKeys.ts`) | Single source of truth for all cache keys |
    13→| **Global UI state** | React Context | Cross-component state (selected project, current shot) |
    14→| **Persisted UI state** | `useUserUIState` | Preferences saved to user settings |
    15→| **Local state** | `useState`/`useReducer` | Component-internal state |
    16→| **URL state** | React Router | Route params, query strings |
    17→
    18→### Query Key Convention
    19→
    20→Keys use **nouns**, **kebab-case** for multi-word, scoped **broad-to-specific**:
    21→`['shots', projectId]` not `[projectId, 'shots']`.
    22→
    23→All keys live in `queryKeys` object. Invalidation goes through hooks in `shared/hooks/invalidation/`, never raw `queryClient.invalidateQueries`.
    24→
    25→---
    26→
    27→## Contexts
    28→
    29→| Context | Provider location |
    30→|---------|-------------------|
    31→| `AuthContext` | `App.tsx` (top-level) |
    32→| `ProjectContext` | `App.tsx` (inside auth) |
    33→| `UserSettingsContext` | `App.tsx` (inside auth) |
    34→| `ShotsContext` | Project route layout |
    35→| `CurrentShotContext` | Shot route layout |
    36→| `PanesContext` | Shot route layout |
    37→| `GenerationTaskContext` | Tool pages |
    38→| `AIInputModeContext` | Tool pages |
    39→| `IncomingTasksContext` | Project route layout |
    40→| `ToolPageHeaderContext` | Tool page layout |
    41→| `LastAffectedShotContext` | Project route layout |
    42→
    43→### Provider nesting order matters
    44→
    45→See `App.tsx` for the hierarchy. Providers that depend on others must be nested inside them (e.g., `ProjectContext` inside `AuthContext`).
    46→
    47→---
    48→
    49→## Cross-Cutting Systems (details in dedicated docs)
    50→
    51→| System | Doc |
    52→|--------|-----|
    53→| Settings (scope cascade, persistence) | [settings_system.md](settings_system.md) |
    54→| Error handling (typed errors, `handleError()`) | [error_handling.md](error_handling.md) |
    55→| Realtime (subscriptions, batching, invalidation) | [realtime_system.md](realtime_system.md) |
    56→| Performance (memoization, preloading, debouncing) | [performance_system.md](performance_system.md) |
    57→| Task creation (validate, transform, insert) | [unified_task_creation.md](unified_task_creation.md) |
    58→| Image loading (progressive, lazy, preload) | [image_loading_system.md](image_loading_system.md) |
    59→| Tool module structure | [adding_new_tool.md](../adding_new_tool.md) |
    60→| Shared utilities (ModalContainer, ConfirmDialog) | [shared_utilities.md](shared_utilities.md) |
```

File doesn't exist (may have been renamed/removed). Let me now check the `OperationSuccess` contract issue:

The `OperationSuccess<T>` type has `recoverable: false` as a fixed field. This is semantically odd: success results don't need a `recoverable` field. It's there presumably to satisfy discriminated union checks, but it creates a confusing API - callers seeing `recoverable: false` on a success result might reasonably ask "what wasn't recoverable?" The contract mixes failure-semantics fields into the success type.

Now let me check the `calculateTaskCost` rounding inconsistency:

In `costHelpers.ts`:
- `calculateVideoEnhanceCost` rounds to 6 decimal places (`Math.round(totalCost * 1000000) / 1000000`)
- `calculateTaskCost` rounds to 3 decimal places (`Math.round(totalCost * 1000) / 1000`)

This is a contract coherence issue: `calculateTaskCost` delegates to `calculateVideoEnhanceCost` for `video_enhance` tasks, which rounds to 6 decimals, but all other billing types round to 3 decimals. Callers can't rely on consistent precision.

```
     9→interface DeprecationSignalOptions {

    11→  policy: DeprecationPolicy;

    13→  enforcement?: 'warn' | 'throw' | 'auto';
    14→}

    19→  }
    20→
    21→  const metaEnv = typeof import.meta !== 'undefined'
    22→    ? (import.meta as unknown as { env?: Record<string, string | undefined> }).env
    23→    : undefined;
    24→  const nodeEnv = typeof process !== 'undefined' ? process.env?.NODE_ENV : undefined;
    25→  const isTestMode = nodeEnv === 'test' || metaEnv?.MODE === 'test' || metaEnv?.VITEST === 'true';
    26→  const explicit = metaEnv?.VITE_DEPRECATION_ENFORCEMENT;
    27→
    28→  if (explicit === 'throw') {

    30→  }
    31→  if (explicit === 'warn') {

    33→  }

    46→export function signalPastRemovalTargetUsage({
    47→  alias,
    48→  policy,

    63→  const message = `[deprecation] ${alias} is past removal target ${policy.removeBy} (owner: ${policy.owner}).${suffix}`;
```

```
1→import { AppError, categorizeError } from './errors';
     2→
     3→interface ErrorNormalizationOptions {
     4→  context: string;
     5→  logData?: Record<string, unknown>;
     6→}
     7→
     8→/**
     9→ * Normalize unknown errors into AppError with structured context.
    10→ * Keep this pure so presentation layers can decide logging/toast behavior.
    11→ */
    12→export function normalizeAppError(
    13→  error: unknown,
    14→  options: ErrorNormalizationOptions
    15→): AppError {
    16→  const { context, logData } = options;
    17→  return categorizeError(error, { context, ...logData });
    18→}
    19→
```

```
    11→
    12→/**
    13→ * Hook to handle mobile video preloading via hidden <video> elements.
    14→ * Creates a preload video element on first tap and exposes the preload function

    17→export function useMobileVideoPreload(
    18→  video: GenerationRow,
    19→  originalIndex: number,
    20→  isMobile: boolean,
    21→  onMobilePreload: ((index: number) => void) | undefined
    22→): { isMobilePreloading: boolean } {
    23→  const [isMobilePreloading, setIsMobilePreloading] = useState(false);
    24→  const preloadVideoRef = useRef<HTMLVideoElement | null>(null);
    25→
    26→  const startMobileVideoPreload = React.useCallback(() => {
    27→    if (!isMobile || isMobilePreloading || preloadVideoRef.current) {
    28→      return;
    29→    }
    30→
    31→    setIsMobilePreloading(true);
    32→
    33→    // Create hidden video element for preloading
    34→    const preloadVideo = document.createElement('video');
    35→    const resolvedSrc = getDisplayUrl((video.location || video.imageUrl || '') as string);
    36→    preloadVideo.src = resolvedSrc;
    37→    preloadVideo.preload = 'auto';
    38→    preloadVideo.muted = true;
    39→    preloadVideo.playsInline = true;
    40→    preloadVideo.style.display = 'none';
    41→    preloadVideo.style.position = 'absolute';
    42→    preloadVideo.style.top = '-9999px';
    43→    preloadVideo.style.left = '-9999px';
    44→
    45→    // Log errors for debugging
    46→    const handleError = () => {
    47→    };
    48→
    49→    preloadVideo.addEventListener('error', handleError);
    50→
    51→    // Store ref and append to DOM (hidden)
    52→    preloadVideoRef.current = preloadVideo;
    53→    document.body.appendChild(preloadVideo);
    54→
    55→    // Cleanup function
    56→    const cleanup = () => {
    57→      if (preloadVideoRef.current) {
    58→        preloadVideoRef.current.removeEventListener('error', handleError);
    59→        if (preloadVideoRef.current.parentNode) {
    60→          preloadVideoRef.current.parentNode.removeChild(preloadVideoRef.current);
    61→        }
    62→        preloadVideoRef.current = null;
    63→      }
    64→    };
    65→
    66→    // Auto-cleanup after 30 seconds if video not opened
    67→    const timeoutId = setTimeout(() => {
    68→      cleanup();
    69→      setIsMobilePreloading(false);
    70→    }, 30000);
    71→
    72→    // Store cleanup function for manual cleanup
    73→    preloadVideo.dataset.cleanupTimeoutId = timeoutId.toString();
    74→
    75→    return cleanup;
    76→  }, [isMobile, isMobilePreloading, video.location, video.imageUrl]);
    77→
    78→  // Cleanup preload video on unmount or video change
    79→  useEffect(() => {
    80→    return () => {
    81→      if (preloadVideoRef.current) {
    82→        const timeoutId = preloadVideoRef.current.dataset.cleanupTimeoutId;
    83→        if (timeoutId) {
    84→          clearTimeout(parseInt(timeoutId));
    85→        }
    86→        if (preloadVideoRef.current.parentNode) {
    87→          preloadVideoRef.current.parentNode.removeChild(preloadVideoRef.current);
    88→        }
    89→        preloadVideoRef.current = null;
    90→      }
    91→    };
    92→  }, [video.location, video.imageUrl]);
    93→
    94→  // Create stable preload handler for this video item
    95→  const handleMobilePreload = React.useCallback(() => {
    96→    startMobileVideoPreload();
    97→  }, [startMobileVideoPreload]);
    98→
    99→  // Expose preload function to parent via global map keyed by originalIndex
   100→  React.useEffect(() => {
   101→    if (onMobilePreload) {

   106→

   109→      };
   110→    }
   111→  }, [originalIndex, handleMobilePreload, onMobilePreload]);
   112→
   113→  return { isMobilePreloading };
   114→}
```

```
1→/**
     2→ * Hook for managing lightbox transition overlay state.
     3→ * Prevents flash when navigating between different lightbox types (image ↔ segment).
     4→ */
     5→
     6→import { useCallback, useEffect, useRef, useState } from 'react';
     7→
     8→interface UseLightboxTransitionReturn {
     9→  /** Whether a transition is currently in progress */
    10→  isLightboxTransitioning: boolean;
    11→  /** Ref for the transition overlay element */
    12→  transitionOverlayRef: React.RefObject<HTMLDivElement>;
    13→  /** Show the overlay synchronously */
    14→  showTransitionOverlay: () => void;
    15→  /** Hide the overlay with fade animation */
    16→  hideTransitionOverlay: () => void;
    17→  /** Execute navigation with transition overlay to prevent flash */
    18→  navigateWithTransition: (doNavigation: () => void) => void;
    19→}
    20→
    21→export function useLightboxTransition(): UseLightboxTransitionReturn {
    22→  // Track lightbox transitions to keep overlay visible during navigation
    23→  const [isLightboxTransitioning, setIsLightboxTransitioning] = useState(false);
    24→
    25→  // Ref for synchronous overlay control (React state updates are async, causing flash)
    26→  const transitionOverlayRef = useRef<HTMLDivElement>(null);
    27→
    28→  // Show overlay synchronously via ref (bypasses React's async state batching)
    29→  const showTransitionOverlay = useCallback(() => {
    30→    if (transitionOverlayRef.current) {
    31→      transitionOverlayRef.current.style.display = 'block';
    32→      transitionOverlayRef.current.style.opacity = '1';
    33→    }
    34→    setIsLightboxTransitioning(true);
    35→  }, []);
    36→
    37→  const hideTransitionOverlay = useCallback(() => {
    38→    if (transitionOverlayRef.current) {
    39→      // Fade out smoothly over 150ms
    40→      transitionOverlayRef.current.style.transition = 'opacity 150ms ease-out';
    41→      transitionOverlayRef.current.style.opacity = '0';
    42→      // Hide after fade completes
    43→      setTimeout(() => {
    44→        if (transitionOverlayRef.current) {
    45→          transitionOverlayRef.current.style.display = 'none';
    46→          transitionOverlayRef.current.style.transition = '';
    47→        }
    48→      }, 150);
    49→    }
    50→    setIsLightboxTransitioning(false);
    51→  }, []);
    52→
    53→  // Helper to navigate with transition overlay - prevents flash when component type changes
    54→  // Shows overlay synchronously, waits for paint via double-rAF, then executes navigation
    55→  const navigateWithTransition = useCallback((doNavigation: () => void) => {
    56→    showTransitionOverlay();
    57→    document.body.classList.add('lightbox-transitioning');
    58→    requestAnimationFrame(() => {
    59→      requestAnimationFrame(() => {
    60→        doNavigation();
    61→      });
    62→    });
    63→  }, [showTransitionOverlay]);
    64→
    65→  // Safety cleanup: always remove the class when transition state is cleared
    66→  useEffect(() => {
    67→    if (!isLightboxTransitioning) {
    68→      document.body.classList.remove('lightbox-transitioning');
    69→    }
    70→  }, [isLightboxTransitioning]);
    71→
    72→  // Safety timeout: remove overlay after 500ms max to prevent it getting stuck
    73→  useEffect(() => {
    74→    if (isLightboxTransitioning) {
    75→      const safetyTimer = setTimeout(() => {
    76→        hideTransitionOverlay();
    77→        document.body.classList.remove('lightbox-transitioning');
    78→      }, 500);
    79→      return () => clearTimeout(safetyTimer);
    80→    }
    81→  }, [isLightboxTransitioning, hideTransitionOverlay]);
    82→
    83→  // Safety: ensure body scroll is restored after lightbox transition ends
    84→  useEffect(() => {
    85→    if (!isLightboxTransitioning) {
    86→      const timer = setTimeout(() => {
    87→        if (document.body.style.overflow === 'hidden' && !document.querySelector('[data-dialog-backdrop]')) {
    88→          document.body.style.overflow = '';
    89→        }
    90→      }, 100);
    91→      return () => clearTimeout(timer);
    92→    }
    93→  }, [isLightboxTransitioning]);
    94→
    95→  return {
    96→    isLightboxTransitioning,
    97→    transitionOverlayRef,
    98→    showTransitionOverlay,
    99→    hideTransitionOverlay,
   100→    navigateWithTransition,
   101→  };
   102→}
   103→
```

```
    21→interface SourceGenerationWithAssociations extends GenerationRow {

    24→
    25→interface UseSourceGenerationReturn {

    29→
    30→/**
    31→ * Hook to fetch and manage source generation (based_on) data
    32→ * Fetches the generation that this media was derived from, plus its primary variant
    33→ */
    34→export const useSourceGeneration = ({
    35→  media
    36→}: UseSourceGenerationParams): UseSourceGenerationReturn => {
    37→  const [sourceGenerationData, setSourceGenerationData] = useState<SourceGenerationWithAssociations | null>(null);
    38→  const [sourcePrimaryVariant, setSourcePrimaryVariant] = useState<SourceVariantData | null>(null);
    39→  const metadataBasedOnId = (media.metadata as Record<string, unknown> | null)?.based_on as string | undefined;
    40→
    41→  useEffect(() => {
    42→    const basedOnId = media.based_on;
    43→    const basedOnFromMetadata = metadataBasedOnId;
    44→
    45→    // Check both direct field and metadata
    46→    const effectiveBasedOnId = basedOnId || basedOnFromMetadata;
    47→    
    48→    if (!effectiveBasedOnId) {
    49→      setSourceGenerationData(null);
    50→      setSourcePrimaryVariant(null);
    51→      return;
    52→    }
    53→    
    54→    const fetchSourceGeneration = async () => {
    55→      try {
    56→        // Fetch source generation with shot associations and primary variant
    57→        // Use left join (no !inner) so we get the generation even if it's not in any shot
    58→        const { data, error } = await supabase().from('generations')
    59→          .select(`

    61→            generation_variants!generation_variants_generation_id_fkey(
    62→              id,
    63→              location,
    64→              thumbnail_url,
    65→              variant_type,
    66→              is_primary
    67→            )
    68→          `)
```

```
1→type ManagedDebugGlobalKey =
     2→  | '__supabase_client__'
     3→  | 'supabase'
     4→  | '__RECONNECT_SCHEDULER__'
     5→  | '__DATA_FRESHNESS_MANAGER__';
     6→
     7→interface ActiveRegistration {
     8→  owner: string;
     9→  value: unknown;
    10→}
    11→
    12→const activeRegistrations = new Map<ManagedDebugGlobalKey, ActiveRegistration>();
    13→
    14→function hasWindow(): boolean {
    15→  return typeof window !== 'undefined';
    16→}
    17→
    18→export function registerDebugGlobal<K extends ManagedDebugGlobalKey>(
    19→  key: K,
    20→  value: NonNullable<Window[K]>,
    21→  owner: string,
    22→): () => void {
    23→  if (!hasWindow()) {
    24→    return () => {};
    25→  }
    26→
    27→  const globalWindow = window as Window;
    28→  const hadPrevious = Object.prototype.hasOwnProperty.call(globalWindow, key);
    29→  const previousValue = globalWindow[key];
    30→  const previousRegistration = activeRegistrations.get(key) ?? null;
    31→
    32→  globalWindow[key] = value;
    33→  activeRegistrations.set(key, { owner, value });
    34→
    35→  let disposed = false;
    36→  return () => {
    37→    if (disposed || !hasWindow()) {
    38→      return;
    39→    }
    40→    disposed = true;
    41→
    42→    const currentRegistration = activeRegistrations.get(key);
    43→    if (!currentRegistration || currentRegistration.value !== value) {
    44→      return;
    45→    }
    46→
    47→    if (previousRegistration) {
    48→      globalWindow[key] = previousRegistration.value as Window[K];
    49→      activeRegistrations.set(key, previousRegistration);
    50→      return;
    51→    }
    52→
    53→    if (hadPrevious) {
    54→      globalWindow[key] = previousValue as Window[K];
    55→    } else {
    56→      delete (globalWindow as Partial<Record<ManagedDebugGlobalKey, unknown>>)[key];
    57→    }
    58→
    59→    activeRegistrations.delete(key);
    60→  };
    61→}
    62→
    63→export function getDebugGlobal<K extends ManagedDebugGlobalKey>(key: K): Window[K] | undefined {
    64→  if (!hasWindow()) {
    65→    return undefined;
    66→  }
    67→  return (window as Window)[key];
    68→}
    69→
    70→export function getDebugGlobalOwner([REDACTED]): string | null {
    71→  return activeRegistrations.get(key)?.owner ?? null;
    72→}
    73→
```

```
    18→function toSettingsRecord(value: Json | null | undefined): Record<string, unknown> | null {

    25→/**

    28→async function fetchProjectGenerationModesFromDB(projectId: string): Promise<Map<string, GenerationModeNormalized>> {
    29→  
    30→  // IMPORTANT:
    31→  // This cache must match the effective settings resolution used by `useToolSettings`:
    32→  // defaults → user → project → shot.
    33→  //
    34→  // If we only look at shots.settings, we will be wrong for shots that inherit
    35→  // generationMode from user/project defaults.
    36→  const { data: sessionData } = await supabase().auth.getSession();

    39→  // Skip queries if user is not authenticated (e.g., on public share pages)
    40→  // RLS will block these queries anyway, causing 406 errors
    41→  if (!userId) {
    42→    return new Map<string, GenerationModeNormalized>();
    43→  }
    44→
    45→  const [userResult, projectResult, shotsResult] = await Promise.all([
    46→    supabase().from('users').select('settings').eq('id', userId).maybeSingle(),
    47→    supabase().from('projects').select('settings').eq('id', projectId).maybeSingle(),
    48→    supabase().from('shots').select('id, settings').eq('project_id', projectId),
    49→  ]);
    50→
    51→  if (shotsResult.error) {
    52→    console.error('[ProjectGenerationModesCache] Error fetching shot settings:', shotsResult.error);
    53→    throw shotsResult.error;
    54→  }
    55→
    56→  const toolId = TOOL_IDS.TRAVEL_BETWEEN_IMAGES;
    57→  const userToolSettings = extractToolSettings(toSettingsRecord(userResult.data?.settings), toolId);
    58→  const projectToolSettings = extractToolSettings(toSettingsRecord(projectResult.data?.settings), toolId);
    59→
    60→  const modes = new Map<string, GenerationModeNormalized>();
    61→  (shotsResult.data || []).forEach((shot) => {

    80→ * Provides instant access to any shot's generation mode within the project
    81→ *
    82→ * @param projectId - The project ID to fetch modes for
    83→ * @param options.enabled - Additional condition to enable the query (default: true)
    84→ */
    85→export function useProjectGenerationModesCache(projectId: string | null, options?: { enabled?: boolean }) {
    86→  const { enabled = true } = options ?? {};
    87→  const cacheRef = useRef(globalProjectGenerationModesCache);
    88→  const queryClient = useQueryClient();
    89→  
    90→  const smartPollingConfig = useSmartPollingConfig(settingsQueryKeys.generationModes(projectId ?? '__no-project__'));
    91→  
    92→  // Query to fetch all shot generation modes for the project
    93→  const { data: projectModes, isLoading, error, refetch } = useQuery<Map<string, GenerationModeNormalized>>({
    94→    [REDACTED](projectId!),
    95→    queryFn: () => fetchProjectGenerationModesFromDB(projectId!),
    96→    enabled: !!projectId && enabled,
    97→    gcTime: 10 * 60 * 1000, // 10 minutes
    98→    placeholderData: (previousData) => previousData, // Keep showing previous data while refetching
    99→    ...smartPollingConfig,
   100→    refetchIntervalInBackground: true, // Enable background polling
   101→  });
   102→  
   103→  // PERF: Ref for projectModes so callbacks always read latest without needing it in deps.
   104→  // Maps break React Query's structural sharing → projectModes is a new reference on every
   105→  // refetch → callbacks with projectModes in deps are recreated → break React.memo on children.
   106→  const projectModesRef = useRef(projectModes);
   107→  projectModesRef.current = projectModes;
   108→
   109→  // Update cache when data changes
   110→  React.useEffect(() => {
   111→    if (projectModes && projectId) {
   112→      cacheRef.current.setProject(projectId, projectModes);
   113→    }
   114→  }, [projectModes, projectId]);
   115→
   116→  const getShotGenerationMode = useCallback((shotId: string | null, isMobile: boolean = false): GenerationModeNormalized | null => {
   117→    // Mobile always uses batch mode
   118→    if (isMobile) {
   119→      return 'batch';
   120→    }
   121→
   122→    if (!projectId || !shotId) return null;
   123→
   124→    // First try cache
   125→    const cachedMode = cacheRef.current.getItem(projectId, shotId);
   126→    if (cachedMode !== null) {
   127→      return cachedMode;
   128→    }
   129→
   130→    // Then try current query data
   131→    const value = projectModesRef.current?.get(shotId);
   132→    return value !== undefined ? value : null;
   133→  }, [projectId]);
   134→
   135→  const getAllShotModes = useCallback((): Map<string, GenerationModeNormalized> | null => {
   136→    if (!projectId) return null;
   137→
   138→    // First try cache
   139→    const cachedModes = cacheRef.current.getProject(projectId);
   140→    if (cachedModes) {
   141→      return cachedModes;
   142→    }
   143→
   144→    // Then try current query data
   145→    return projectModesRef.current || null;
   146→  }, [projectId]);
   147→  
   148→  const clearCache = useCallback((): void => {
   149→    cacheRef.current.clear();
   150→  }, []);
   151→  
   152→  const deleteProjectCache = useCallback((projectId: string | null): void => {
   153→    if (!projectId) return;
   154→    cacheRef.current.deleteProject(projectId);
   155→  }, []);
   156→  
   157→  // Debug function to log cache state
   158→  const logCacheState = useCallback((): void => {
   159→  }, []);
   160→  
   161→  // Optimistically update a single shot's mode in cache
   162→  const updateShotMode = useCallback((shotId: string | null, mode: GenerationModeNormalized) => {
   163→    if (!projectId || !shotId) return;
   164→    
   165→    // Update in-memory cache immediately
   166→    const currentModes = cacheRef.current.getProject(projectId);
   167→    if (currentModes) {
   168→      currentModes.set(shotId, mode);
   169→      cacheRef.current.setProject(projectId, currentModes);
   170→    }
   171→    
   172→    // CRITICAL: Also update React Query cache so it persists across re-renders
   173→    // The previous code created updatedModes but never saved it!
   174→    queryClient.setQueryData<Map<string, GenerationModeNormalized>>(
   175→      settingsQueryKeys.generationModes(projectId!),
   176→      (oldData) => {
   177→        if (!oldData) return oldData;
   178→        const newData = new Map(oldData);
   179→        newData.set(shotId, mode);
   180→        return newData;
   181→      }
   182→    );
   183→  }, [projectId, queryClient]);
   184→  
   185→  // Invalidate cache when mode changes (for manual refresh if needed)
   186→  const invalidateOnModeChange = useCallback(() => {
   187→    if (projectId) {
   188→      cacheRef.current.deleteProject(projectId);
   189→      refetch();
   190→    }
   191→  }, [projectId, refetch]);
   192→
   193→  return {
   194→    getShotGenerationMode,
   195→    getAllShotModes,
   196→    updateShotMode,
   197→    isLoading,
   198→    error,
   199→    refetch,
   200→    clearCache,
   201→    deleteProjectCache,
   202→    invalidateOnModeChange,
   203→    logCacheState
   204→  };
   205→}
   206→
```

```
   152→  navigate: (path: string) => void;
   153→  scheduleTimeout: ScheduleTimeout;
   154→}) {
   155→  const {
   156→    completeTour,
   157→    skipTour,
   158→    setIsGenerationsPaneLocked,
   159→    setIsTasksPaneLocked,
   160→    setStepIndex,
   161→    setIsPaused,
   162→    navigate,
   163→    scheduleTimeout,
   164→  } = input;
   165→
   166→  return useCallback((data: CallBackProps) => {
   167→    const { status, index, type, action } = data;
   168→
   169→    if (type === EVENTS.STEP_AFTER || type === EVENTS.TARGET_NOT_FOUND) {
   170→      const nextIndex = index + (action === ACTIONS.PREV ? -1 : 1);
   171→
   172→      if (index === TOUR_STEPS.OPEN_GALLERY && action !== ACTIONS.PREV) {
   173→        setIsGenerationsPaneLocked(true);
   174→        pauseThenAdvance(nextIndex, setStepIndex, setIsPaused, SHORT_DELAY_MS, scheduleTimeout);
   175→      } else if (index === TOUR_STEPS.GALLERY_SECTION && action !== ACTIONS.PREV) {
   176→        setStepIndex(nextIndex);
   177→      } else if (index === TOUR_STEPS.GENERATE_IMAGES && action !== ACTIONS.PREV) {
   178→        dispatchTourEvent('openGenerationModal');
   179→        pauseThenAdvance(nextIndex, setStepIndex, setIsPaused, SHORT_DELAY_MS, scheduleTimeout);
   180→      } else if (index === TOUR_STEPS.HOW_IT_WORKS && action !== ACTIONS.PREV) {
   181→        dispatchTourEvent('closeGenerationModal');
   182→        setIsGenerationsPaneLocked(false);
   183→        setIsPaused(true);
   184→        scheduleTimeout(() => {
   185→          const waitForTarget = () => {
   186→            const target = document.querySelector('[data-tour="first-shot"]');
   187→            if (target) {
   188→              setStepIndex(nextIndex);
   189→              scheduleTimeout(() => setIsPaused(false), 100);
   190→            } else {
   191→              scheduleTimeout(waitForTarget, 100);
   192→            }
   193→          };
   194→          waitForTarget();
   195→        }, WAIT_FOR_TARGET_DELAY_MS);
   196→      } else if (index === TOUR_STEPS.OPEN_FIRST_SHOT && action !== ACTIONS.PREV) {
   197→        const firstShot = document.querySelector('[data-tour="first-shot"]') as HTMLElement;
   198→        if (firstShot) {
   199→          firstShot.click();
   200→        }
   201→        pauseThenAdvance(nextIndex, setStepIndex, setIsPaused, LONG_DELAY_MS, scheduleTimeout);
   202→      } else if (index === TOUR_STEPS.TASKS_PANE && action !== ACTIONS.PREV) {
   203→        setIsTasksPaneLocked(true);
   204→        pauseThenAdvance(nextIndex, setStepIndex, setIsPaused, SHORT_DELAY_MS, scheduleTimeout);
   205→      } else {
   206→        setStepIndex(nextIndex);
   207→      }
   208→    }
   209→
   210→    if (status === STATUS.FINISHED) {
   211→      completeTour();
   212→      navigate(TOOL_ROUTES.TRAVEL_BETWEEN_IMAGES);
   213→    } else if (status === STATUS.SKIPPED) {
   214→      skipTour();
   215→    }
   216→  }, [
   217→    completeTour,
   218→    navigate,
   219→    setIsGenerationsPaneLocked,
   220→    setIsPaused,
   221→    setIsTasksPaneLocked,
   222→    setStepIndex,
   223→    scheduleTimeout,
   224→    skipTour,
   225→  ]);
   226→}
   227→
   228→export function ProductTour() {
   229→  const { isRunning, completeTour, skipTour } = useProductTour();
   230→  const { setIsGenerationsPaneLocked, setIsTasksPaneLocked, resetAllPaneLocks } = usePanes();
   231→  const navigate = useNavigate();
   232→  const { scheduleTimeout, clearScheduledTimeouts } = useManagedTimeouts();
   233→  const { stepIndex, setStepIndex, isPaused, setIsPaused } = useTourProgressState(
   234→    isRunning,
   235→    resetAllPaneLocks
   236→  );
   237→
   238→  useEffect(() => {
   239→    if (!isRunning) {
   240→      clearScheduledTimeouts();
   241→    }
   242→  }, [clearScheduledTimeouts, isRunning]);
   243→
   244→  useSpotlightClickAdvance({
   245→    isRunning,
   246→    isPaused,
   247→    stepIndex,
   248→    setStepIndex,
   249→    setIsPaused,
   250→    setIsTasksPaneLocked,
   251→    scheduleTimeout,
   252→  });
   253→
   254→  const handleCallback = useJoyrideCallback({
   255→    completeTour,
   256→    skipTour,
   257→    setIsGenerationsPaneLocked,
   258→    setIsTasksPaneLocked,
   259→    setStepIndex,
   260→    setIsPaused,
   261→    navigate,
   262→    scheduleTimeout,
   263→  });
   264→
   265→  if (!isRunning) {
   266→    return null;
   267→  }
   268→
   269→  return (
   270→    <Joyride
   271→      steps={tourSteps}
   272→      run={isRunning && !isPaused}
   273→      stepIndex={stepIndex}
   274→      continuous
   275→      scrollToFirstStep
   276→      showSkipButton
   277→      showProgress
   278→      disableCloseOnEsc={false}
   279→      disableOverlayClose
   280→      callback={handleCallback}
   281→      tooltipComponent={CustomTooltip}
   282→      styles={{
   283→        options: {
   284→          zIndex: 100010,
   285→          arrowColor: 'hsl(var(--background))',
   286→        },
   287→        spotlight: {
   288→          borderRadius: 8,
   289→          transition: 'opacity 0.3s ease, transform 0.3s ease',
   290→        },
   291→        overlay: {
   292→          backgroundColor: 'hsl(0 0% 0% / 0.5)',
   293→          transition: 'opacity 0.3s ease',
   294→        },
   295→      }}
   296→      floaterProps={{
   297→        styles: {
   298→          floater: {
   299→            filter: 'drop-shadow(0 4px 12px hsl(0 0% 0% / 0.15))',
   300→            transition: 'opacity 0.3s ease, transform 0.3s ease',
   301→          },
   302→        },
   303→      }}
   304→    />
   305→  );
   306→}
```

```
1→# Frontend Architecture Patterns
     2→
     3→---
     4→
     5→## State Management
     6→
     7→No Redux/Zustand. State flows through specific layers:
     8→
     9→| Layer | Tool | Purpose |
    10→|-------|------|---------|
    11→| **Server state** | React Query | Remote data (shots, generations, settings) |
    12→| **Query keys** | `queryKeys` registry (`shared/lib/queryKeys.ts`) | Single source of truth for all cache keys |
    13→| **Global UI state** | React Context | Cross-component state (selected project, current shot) |
    14→| **Persisted UI state** | `useUserUIState` | Preferences saved to user settings |
    15→| **Local state** | `useState`/`useReducer` | Component-internal state |
    16→| **URL state** | React Router | Route params, query strings |
    17→
    18→### Query Key Convention
    19→
    20→Keys use **nouns**, **kebab-case** for multi-word, scoped **broad-to-specific**:
    21→`['shots', projectId]` not `[projectId, 'shots']`.
    22→
    23→All keys live in `queryKeys` object. Invalidation goes through hooks in `shared/hooks/invalidation/`, never raw `queryClient.invalidateQueries`.
    24→
    25→---
    26→
    27→## Contexts
    28→
    29→| Context | Provider location |
    30→|---------|-------------------|
    31→| `AuthContext` | `App.tsx` (top-level) |
    32→| `ProjectContext` | `App.tsx` (inside auth) |
    33→| `UserSettingsContext` | `App.tsx` (inside auth) |
    34→| `ShotsContext` | Project route layout |
    35→| `CurrentShotContext` | Shot route layout |
    36→| `PanesContext` | Shot route layout |
    37→| `GenerationTaskContext` | Tool pages |
    38→| `AIInputModeContext` | Tool pages |
    39→| `IncomingTasksContext` | Project route layout |
    40→| `ToolPageHeaderContext` | Tool page layout |
    41→| `LastAffectedShotContext` | Project route layout |
    42→
    43→### Provider nesting order matters
    44→
    45→See `App.tsx` for the hierarchy. Providers that depend on others must be nested inside them (e.g., `ProjectContext` inside `AuthContext`).
    46→
    47→---

    50→
```

3. `mobileProjectDebug.ts` - attaches to `window` at module scope (import-time side effect)
4. `simpleCacheValidator.ts` - attaches to `window` at module scope (import-time side effect)
5. `logger.ts` - captures `console.log/warn/error` at module scope; ordering matters relative to any other console-overwriting code
6. `__IS_DEV_ENV__` in `env.ts` - computed constant at import time that reads `window.location.hostname`; consumers use the stale snapshot instead of a function call
7. `settingsWriteQueue.ts` - `enqueueSettingsWrite` throws if `setSettingsWriteFunction` wasn't called first - implicit boot ordering dependency
8. `DataFreshnessManager`, `RealtimeEventProcessor`, `queryClient` - module-scope singletons instantiated at import time

The dynamically-imported debug tools (items 1-4) are all guarded by `import.meta.env.DEV` and loaded lazily from bootstrap, which mitigates but doesn't eliminate the coupling. The more significant findings are the `originalConsole` capture ordering, the `__IS_DEV_ENV__` snapshot constant, and the `settingsWriteQueue` boot-order dependency.

The codebase has a well-designed error infrastructure (`AppError` hierarchy, `normalizeAndPresentError`, `OperationResult`) that is used consistently in the majority of files (~300+ files use `normalizeAndPresentError`). However, there are meaningful inconsistencies:

4. **Silent failures** - `useReplaceInShot` and `useShareGeneration` swallow DB errors with no user feedback and limited/no logging.

5. **Typed errors underused** - The `AuthError`/`NetworkError`/`ServerError` hierarchy exists but only ~12 throw sites use it vs ~214 using bare `new Error`, relying on message-string-matching in `categorizeError()` to reconstruct types.

I reviewed the codebase for the `initialization_coupling` dimension, which covers boot-order dependencies, import-time side effects, global singletons, and environment variable reads at module scope.

**Score: 78/100**

The codebase shows strong discipline in most initialization patterns. The Supabase client uses a proper lazy singleton with a Result-type accessor. Debug config, toast runtime, viewport lock runtime, and error presenter all use explicit `initialize*()` / `install*()` patterns called from a well-structured bootstrap sequence in `/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/reigh/src/app/bootstrap.tsx`. Environment config in `env.ts` correctly uses lazy getters for critical values.

All are dynamically imported and dev-only, which mitigates risk but breaks the pattern established elsewhere.

5. **Module-scope singletons** in `DataFreshnessManager`, `RealtimeEventProcessor`, `queryClient`, `TimestampManager` -- low risk since constructors are self-contained, but inconsistent with the lazy-getter pattern used by peer modules.

I've now completed a thorough review. Let me summarize findings and write the output.

Key observations:
1. **Strong centralized auth infrastructure**: `edgeHandler.ts` provides consistent `bootstrapEdgeHandler`/`withEdgeRequest` wrappers used by all edge functions. The `auth.ts` module provides reusable `authenticateRequest`, `verifyTaskOwnership`, `verifyShotOwnership`, and `getTaskUserId`.
2. **Consistent auth enforcement**: All 32 edge functions use the shared bootstrap, and all require auth (except `stripe-webhook` which uses Stripe signature verification instead).
3. **Ownership verification**: Functions consistently verify ownership for non-service-role callers through project ownership checks.
4. **RLS coverage**: All core tables have RLS enabled with appropriate policies.
5. **One notable inconsistency**: The `grant-credits` function allows any authenticated user to call the welcome bonus path for themselves. The `isWelcomeBonus` flag is client-controlled, which means a JWT-authenticated user could potentially call `grant-credits` with `isWelcomeBonus: true` and their own `userId` to get credits - though the atomic `given_credits` flag prevents this from being exploited more than once.
6. **Minor inconsistency**: Some worker-only functions that don't need JWT auth don't specify `allowJwtUserAuth`, while user-facing functions do. This is intentionally different but could be more explicitly documented.

```
    23→    // Fix: replace PostgrestClient.fetch (a public property, read dynamically on
    24→    // every from()/rpc() call) with a version that injects the cached token
    25→    // directly, bypassing getSession/navigator.locks entirely for data requests.
    26→    // Auth operations (supabase.auth.*) are unaffected.

    35→        persistSession: true,
    36→        detectSessionInUrl: true,
    37→      },
    38→      realtime: {
    39→        params: { eventsPerSecond: 10 },
    40→        heartbeatIntervalMs: REALTIME_HEARTBEAT_INTERVAL_MS,
    41→        reconnectAfterMs: (tries: number) => Math.min(tries * 1000, REALTIME_MAX_RECONNECT_DELAY_MS),

    44→        fetch: fetchWithTimeout,
    45→      },

    49→    // Replace PostgrestClient.fetch to use the cached token.
    50→    // PostgrestClient reads this.fetch on each from()/rpc() call, so the
    51→    // replacement takes effect immediately without recreating any clients.
    52→    const dataFetch = (input: RequestInfo | URL, init: RequestInit = {}): Promise<Response> => {
    53→      const headers = new Headers(init.headers ?? {});

    61→    (client as unknown as { rest: { fetch: typeof dataFetch } }).rest.fetch = dataFetch;
```

2. Key Technical Concepts:
   - **Desloppify**: Codebase health scanner with scoring: `40% mechanical + 60% subjective = overall`
   - **Strict score**: North star metric where wontfix items count as open (penalized)
   - **Subjective review workflow**: `desloppify review --prepare` → launch blind subagents → `desloppify review --import merged.json --manual-override --attest "..."  --scan-after-import`
   - **Blind packet**: `.desloppify/review_packet_blind.json` — no score targets to prevent anchoring
   - **Plan vs Review**: Plan queue tracks what to fix; review system tracks subjective dimension scores. They're separate — resolving plan items does NOT update subjective scores
   - **Investigation batches**: Pre-structured one-per-dimension with seed files in `investigation_batches`
   - **Claude overlay docs**: `/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/desloppify/docs/CLAUDE.md` describes the subagent review workflow

4. Errors and fixes:

3. **inconsistent-jwt-auth-allowance** (low confidence): Worker-facing vs user-facing functions have different `allowJwtUserAuth` settings without documentation distinguishing the two categories.

```
1→/**
     2→ * Best-effort clipboard write that never throws.
     3→ * Returns true when the write succeeds.
     4→ */
     5→export async function writeClipboardTextSafe(
     6→  text: string,
     7→  options: { allowExecCommandFallback?: boolean } = {},
     8→): Promise<boolean> {
     9→  if (!text) {
    10→    return false;
    11→  }
    12→
    13→  if (typeof navigator !== 'undefined' && navigator.clipboard?.writeText) {
    14→    try {
    15→      await navigator.clipboard.writeText(text);
    16→      return true;
    17→    } catch {
    18→      // fall through to optional fallback
    19→    }
    20→  }
    21→
    22→  if (!options.allowExecCommandFallback || typeof document === 'undefined') {
    23→    return false;
    24→  }
    25→
    26→  let textarea: HTMLTextAreaElement | null = null;
    27→  try {
    28→    textarea = document.createElement('textarea');
    29→    textarea.value = text;
    30→    textarea.style.position = 'fixed';
    31→    textarea.style.left = '-9999px';
    32→    document.body.appendChild(textarea);
    33→    textarea.select();
    34→    return document.execCommand('copy') === true;
    35→  } catch {
    36→    return false;
    37→  } finally {
    38→    if (textarea?.parentNode) {
    39→      textarea.parentNode.removeChild(textarea);
    40→    }
    41→  }
    42→}
    43→
```

```
1→export const fileToDataURL = (file: File): Promise<string> =>
     2→  new Promise((resolve, reject) => {
     3→    const reader = new FileReader();
     4→    reader.onload = () => resolve(reader.result as string);
     5→    reader.onerror = (error) => reject(error);
     6→    reader.readAsDataURL(file);
     7→  });
     8→
     9→export const dataURLtoFile = (
    10→  dataUrl: string,
    11→  filename: string,
    12→  fileType?: string
    13→): File | null => {
    14→  try {
    15→    const [metadata, payload] = dataUrl.split(',');
    16→    if (!metadata || !payload) {
    17→      throw new Error('Invalid Data URL format');
    18→    }
    19→
    20→    const mimeMatch = metadata.match(/:(.*?);/);
    21→    const mimeType =
    22→      fileType ||
    23→      (mimeMatch && mimeMatch[1]) ||
    24→      'application/octet-stream';
    25→    const decodedPayload = atob(payload);
    26→    const bytes = new Uint8Array(decodedPayload.length);
    27→
    28→    for (let i = 0; i < decodedPayload.length; i += 1) {
    29→      bytes[i] = decodedPayload.charCodeAt(i);
    30→    }
    31→
    32→    return new File([bytes], filename, { type: mimeType });
    33→  } catch {
    34→    return null;
    35→  }
    36→};
    37→
```

```
    30→function resolveTaskScopeProjectId(projectId: string | null): string | null {
    31→  if (projectId && projectId.trim().length > 0) {
    32→    return projectId;
    33→  }
    34→  const selectedProjectId = getProjectSelectionFallbackId();
    35→  if (selectedProjectId && selectedProjectId.trim().length > 0) {
    36→    return selectedProjectId;
    37→  }
    38→  return null;
    39→}
    40→
    41→/**
    42→ * Preload task mappings for a batch of generations in the background.
    43→ */
    44→export async function preloadGenerationTaskMappings(
    45→  queryClient: QueryClient,
    46→  generationIds: string[],
    47→  projectId: string | null,
    48→  options: PreloadGenerationTaskMappingsOptions = {},
    49→) {
    50→  const supabase = getSupabaseClient();
    51→  const effectiveProjectId = resolveTaskScopeProjectId(projectId);
    52→  const {
    53→    batchSize = 5,
    54→    delayBetweenBatches = 200,
    55→    preloadFullTaskData = false,
    56→  } = options;
    57→
    58→  for (let i = 0; i < generationIds.length; i += batchSize) {
    59→    const batch = generationIds.slice(i, i + batchSize);
    60→
    61→    const mappings = await getPrimaryTaskMappingsForGenerations(batch, { projectId: effectiveProjectId ?? undefined });
    62→    let reportedBatchQueryFailure = false;
    63→
    64→    const prefetchTasks: Array<Promise<unknown>> = [];
    65→
    66→    batch.forEach((generationId) => {
    67→      const mapping = mappings.get(generationId);
    68→      const cacheEntry = toGenerationTaskMappingCacheEntry(mapping);
    69→      queryClient.setQueryData<GenerationTaskMappingCacheEntry>(
    70→        taskQueryKeys.generationMapping(generationId),
    71→        cacheEntry,
    72→      );
    73→
    74→      if (!reportedBatchQueryFailure && cacheEntry.status === 'query_failed' && cacheEntry.queryError) {
    75→        reportedBatchQueryFailure = true;
    76→        normalizeAndPresentError(new Error(cacheEntry.queryError), {
    77→          context: 'GenerationTaskCache',
    78→          showToast: false,
    79→        });
    80→      }
    81→
    82→      if (preloadFullTaskData && effectiveProjectId && cacheEntry.taskId && cacheEntry.status === 'ok') {
    83→        prefetchTasks.push(queryClient.prefetchQuery({
    84→          [REDACTED](cacheEntry.taskId, effectiveProjectId),
    85→          queryFn: async () => {
    86→            const { data, error } = await supabase
    87→              .from('tasks')
    88→              .select('*')
    89→              .eq('id', cacheEntry.taskId)
    90→              .eq('project_id', effectiveProjectId)
    91→              .single();
    92→
    93→            if (error) throw error;
    94→            if (!isTaskDbRow(data)) {
    95→              throw new Error('Task row has unexpected shape');
    96→            }
    97→            return mapTaskDbRowToTask(data);
    98→          },
    99→          staleTime: 2 * 60 * 1000,
   100→        }));
   101→      }
   102→    });
   103→
   104→    if (prefetchTasks.length > 0) {
   105→      await Promise.all(prefetchTasks);
   106→    }
   107→
   108→    if (i + batchSize < generationIds.length) {
   109→      await new Promise((resolve) => setTimeout(resolve, delayBetweenBatches));
   110→    }
   111→  }
   112→}
   113→
   114→export function mergeGenerationsWithTaskData(
   115→  generations: GenerationRow[],
   116→  queryClient: QueryClient,
   117→  projectId: string | null,
   118→): GenerationWithTaskData[] {
   119→  const effectiveProjectId = resolveTaskScopeProjectId(projectId);
   120→
   121→  return generations.map((generation) => {
   122→    const generationId = getGenerationId(generation);
   123→    const cachedMapping = queryClient.getQueryData<GenerationTaskMappingCacheEntry>(
   124→      taskQueryKeys.generationMapping(generationId),
   125→    );
   126→    const taskId = cachedMapping?.taskId || null;
   127→    const taskData = (taskId && effectiveProjectId)
   128→      ? queryClient.getQueryData<Task>(taskQueryKeys.single(taskId, effectiveProjectId))
   129→      : null;
   130→    const taskMappingStatus = cachedMapping?.status ?? (taskId ? 'ok' : 'not_loaded');
   131→
   132→    return {
   133→      ...generation,
   134→      taskId,
   135→      taskData,
   136→      taskMappingStatus,
   137→      ...(cachedMapping?.queryError ? { taskMappingError: cachedMapping.queryError } : {}),
   138→    };
   139→  });
   140→}
```

```
    40→export function useAdjustedTaskDetails({

    48→  const { variantSourceTaskId, variantHasOrchestratorDetails } = useMemo(() => {
    49→    const variantParams = activeVariant?.params as Record<string, unknown> | undefined;
    50→    return {
    51→      variantSourceTaskId: getSourceTaskIdLegacyCompatible(variantParams),
    52→      variantHasOrchestratorDetails: hasOrchestratorDetails(variantParams),
    53→    };
    54→  }, [activeVariant?.params]);
    55→
    56→  // Fetch the variant's source task when it differs from taskDetailsData
    57→  // Skip fetch if variant already has orchestrator_details (e.g., clip_join variants)
    58→  // NOTE: Uses ['tasks', 'single', taskId] query key to share cache with usePrefetchTaskData
    59→  const { data: variantSourceTask, isLoading: isLoadingVariantTask } = useQuery({
    60→    [REDACTED](variantSourceTaskId ?? '', projectId ?? null),
    61→    queryFn: async () => {
    62→      if (!variantSourceTaskId || !projectId) return null;
    63→      const { data, error } = await supabase().from('tasks')
    64→        .select('*')
    65→        .eq('id', variantSourceTaskId)
    66→        .eq('project_id', projectId)
    67→        .single();
    68→      if (error) {
    69→        console.error('[VariantTaskDetails] Error fetching source task:', error);
    70→        return null;
    71→      }
    72→      return data;
    73→    },
    74→    // Don't fetch if: no task ID, already have matching taskDetailsData, or variant has orchestrator_details
    75→    enabled: !!variantSourceTaskId
    76→      && !!projectId
    77→      && variantSourceTaskId !== taskDetailsData?.taskId
    78→      && !variantHasOrchestratorDetails,
    79→    staleTime: Infinity, // Task data is immutable - cache forever (matches prefetch)
    80→  });
    81→
    82→  // For variants, show the variant's source task params instead of the original task
    83→  // But ALWAYS preserve onApplySettingsFromTask so the Apply button shows
    84→  const adjustedTaskDetailsData = useMemo(() => {
    85→    // Check if we're viewing a variant that was created by a task (has source_task_id in params)
    86→    const variantParams = activeVariant?.params as Record<string, unknown> | undefined;
    87→    const isTaskCreatedVariant = activeVariant && variantParams && (

   105→      let effectiveParams = variantParams;

   123→      // Extract input images using shared utility

   125→      const variantInputImages = deriveInputImages(effectiveParams);

   127→      return {
   128→        task: {

   130→          taskType: effectiveTaskType,
   131→          params: effectiveParams,
   132→          status: 'Complete' as Task['status'],

   134→          projectId: '',
   135→        } as Task,
   136→        isLoading: isLoadingVariantTask,
   137→        error: null,
   138→        inputImages: variantInputImages,
   139→        taskId: sourceTaskId ?? activeVariant.id,
   140→        // ALWAYS preserve onApplySettingsFromTask so Apply button shows for all variants
   141→        onApplySettingsFromTask: taskDetailsData?.onApplySettingsFromTask,
   142→      };
   143→    }
   144→
   145→    // If variants are still loading AND we don't have task data yet, show loading
   146→    // But if we already have task data cached, show it immediately rather than blocking on variants
   147→    // This provides better UX when task data is prefetched/cached
   148→    // ALSO check if we're waiting for initialVariantId to be applied (clicked a specific variant)
   149→    const waitingForInitialVariant = initialVariantId &&
   150→      (!activeVariant || activeVariant.id !== initialVariantId);
   151→
   152→    // Only override to loading if:
   153→    // 1. Waiting for a specific variant (user clicked a variant)
   154→    // 2. Variants loading AND no active variant AND task details still loading
   155→    //    (If task details finished - either has task or knows there's none - don't block on variants)
   156→    const shouldShowLoading = waitingForInitialVariant ||

   161→    }
   162→
   163→    // For all other cases, use the generation's task details as-is
   164→    return taskDetailsData;
   165→  }, [taskDetailsData, activeVariant, variantSourceTask, isLoadingVariantTask, isLoadingVariants, initialVariantId]);
   166→
   167→  return {
   168→    adjustedTaskDetailsData,
   169→    isLoadingVariantTask,
   170→  };
   171→}
```

```
    23→/**
```
